subject: arts-music
essential_question: How do extended techniques and larger forms sustain a longer musical idea?
standards: Michigan Arts Education Standards: Music — Creating
project_brief: Compose or produce an extended original work with score or session documentation and analytical commentary. This is the grade 11 culminating project for "Advanced Composition, Production, and Literacy" (ma-g11-arts-and-music-u02, unit 2), built around extended harmonic and modal materials, counterpoint and texture, advanced form and development, production and engineering choices, and score preparation and accessible notation. Compose or produce an extended original work with score or session documentation and analytical commentary. Work only from a public-domain source, an original passage you compose, or material your facilitator has already cleared — never a copyrighted score or recording reproduced in full.
requirements: Address every topic listed for this unit: extended harmonic and modal materials, counterpoint and texture, advanced form and development, production and engineering choices, score preparation and accessible notation, and analysis of original and public-domain works.
Meet the performance task as written: Compose or produce an extended original work with score or session documentation and analytical commentary.
Show your work or process, not just a final result — a process note, sketch log, commit history, or draft trail.
Complete the checklist in this package before submitting.
primary_task: Compose or produce an extended original work with score or session documentation and analytical commentary. Work only from a public-domain source, an original passage you compose, or material your facilitator has already cleared — never a copyrighted score or recording reproduced in full.
critique_criteria: A named viewer, listener, or reader can point to a specific choice in the work and connect it back to extended harmonic and modal materials or another named topic from this unit.
The piece shows at least one deliberate revision — a version-two decision made because the first attempt did not achieve the intended effect.
The student can explain the intended effect on an audience in their own words, separate from just describing what was made.
Only the student's own original work, public-domain material, or a properly licensed and cited excerpt appears in the piece — no unlicensed lyrics, sheet music, or protected work is reproduced.

The submitted evidence (written account, notation, recording made for the student's own review, or live demonstration to the facilitator) is sufficient for a reviewer who was not present to judge the criteria above.

presentation_and_privacy.presentation_options: Sharing this project publicly is always optional and never required for full credit. You may present live to a small audience of your choosing, present privately to just your facilitator, submit a recording made only for your own review, or submit a written/described account of the finished work instead.
presentation_and_privacy.text_or_no_audio_alternative: If any part of this task could involve singing, speaking on camera, or being recorded, you may instead notate the piece, write a detailed description or script, use body percussion or an instrument in place of your voice, or perform live for your facilitator with no recording made at all. No lesson in this unit requires a voice recording, a camera, or a photo.

copyright_and_authorship: The final submitted work must remain your own authorship. A parent, tutor, or AI assistant may help you plan, explain a concept, demonstrate a technique, or give feedback on a draft, but may not produce the graded work itself. Use only your own original work, public-domain material, or a properly licensed and cited excerpt — never reproduce full copyrighted lyrics, sheet music, or another protected work without the rights to do so.
remediation: If the piece isn't coming together, return to a single, smaller exercise focused only on extended harmonic and modal materials, revisit one worked example or model from this unit, and rebuild your confidence with that one element before returning to the full project.
extension: Once the core piece is finished, create a second short variation that explores counterpoint and texture from a different angle, or write a short artist's statement comparing your original intent with what the finished work actually communicates.
